extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of PARI/GP (computational number theorists and mathematicians needing linear algebra and number-theory library routines)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for PARI/GP library functions (substitution, sums, Taylor, Thue solver, and a large collection of vector/matrix/linear-algebra utilities). Each entry describes purpose, allowed input types, flags/options, algorithmic notes and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: substpol(x, y, z)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replace the “variable” y by the argument z in the polynomial expression x. y may be any polynomial; substitution is done by reducing components of x modulo y - t (t new variable) then substituting t by z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All types allowed for x; behaves like subst when y is a variable. Examples: substpol(x^4+x^2+1,x^2,y) -> y^2+y+1; substpol(x^4+x^2+1,x^3,y) -> x^2 + y*x + 1. Library syntax: GEN gsubstpol(GEN x, GEN y, GEN z). Note: gdeflate attempts to detect t(x^d) forms and may return NULL if fails.

rubrics_metrics.name: substvec(x, v, w)
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneously replace each monomial-variable vi in expression x by wi, where v is a vector of degree-1 monomials (variables) and w is a vector of same length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitutions are simultaneous: vi first replaced by new variables, then replaced by wi. Examples: substvec([x,y],[x,y],[y,x]) -> [y,x]; substvec([x,y],[x,y],[y,x+y]) -> [y,x+y] (not [y,2*y]). Library syntax: GEN gsubstvec(GEN x, GEN v, GEN w).

rubrics_metrics.name: sumformal(f, {v})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a polynomial F in v (vanishing at 0) such that F(b)-F(a)= sum_{v=a+1..b} f(v). If v omitted, sum with respect to main variable. Base ring assumed characteristic zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works by treating f as a polynomial function in v and returning an antiderivative polynomial F (polynomial discrete sum). Examples: sumformal(n) -> 1/2*n^2+1/2*n; sumformal(n^3+n^2+1) -> 1/4*n^4+5/6*n^3+3/4*n^2+7/6*n; library syntax: GEN sumformal(GEN f, long v = -1). Use subst to evaluate at bounds for numeric sums.

rubrics_metrics.name: taylor(x, t, {d = seriesprecision})
rubrics_metrics.description: Taylor expansion of x around 0 with respect to variable t to precision d; x can be many types (e.g., rational function). Adds O(t^d) to components (unlike Ser which uses valuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrasts with Ser (which enforces main-variable priority). Example: taylor(x/(1+y), y, 5) -> (y^4 - y^3 + y^2 - y + 1)*x + O(y^5). Library syntax: GEN tayl(GEN x, long t, long precdl). Be mindful of variable priority and precision-related errors (Ser may error if variable priority wrong).

rubrics_metrics.name: thue(tnf, a, {sol})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return all integer solutions (x,y) of P(x,y)=a where tnf was created by thueinit(P). If tnf computed assuming GRH, results may be conditional (except some cases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input may be tnf or polynomial P (then thueinit(P,0) performed implicitly—wasteful for multiple a). If infinite solutions exist, error issued. When tnf computed with GRH assumption, results conditional unless special cases (e.g., a=±1 or reducible P). Examples and demonstration solving x^13-5y^13=-4. Library syntax: GEN thue(GEN tnf, GEN a, GEN sol = NULL). Note: conditionality criteria involve class number h and regulator R estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: thueinit(P, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Initialize the tnf (Thue number field data) for univariate integer polynomial P to be used by thue. flag non-zero requests unconditional certification (no GRH assumption).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=0, uses GRH (faster) and results may be conditional; flag non-zero attempts unconditional certification (slower). Reducible or many cases yield unconditional results even with flag=0. Library syntax: GEN thueinit(GEN P, long flag, long prec).

rubrics_metrics.name: algdep(x, k, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given real/complex/p-adic x, find an integer-coefficient polynomial of degree ≤k having x as approximate root (not necessarily irreducible or the 'correct' one).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internally uses lindep; flag modifies precision/truncation heuristics (flag>0 truncates input). Accuracy of input affects correctness and runtime. Examples show sensitivity to working precision; increasing precision yields correct results. Library syntax: GEN algdep0(GEN x, long k, long flag) or GEN algdep(GEN x, long k). Use subst or polroots to check closeness/roots.

rubrics_metrics.name: charpoly(A, {v = x}, {flag = 5})
rubrics_metrics.description: Characteristic polynomial of A with respect to variable v (det(v*I - A)). If A not square, returns characteristic polynomial of multiplication-by-A map if A is scalar-like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag selects algorithm: 0 Le Verrier (needs n! invertible, O(n^4)); 1 Lagrange interpolation (O(n^4)); 2 Hessenberg (requires field, O(n^3), prone to coefficient explosion); 3 Berkowitz (division-free, O(n^4), valid over any ring); 4 modular algorithm for integral x; 5 (default) auto-selects best method (Berkowitz generally, except Z or safe fields). Examples and alternate named functions (carhess/carberkowitz/caradj). Library syntax: GEN charpoly0(GEN A, long v = -1, long flag). Advice: stick to default flag.

rubrics_metrics.name: concat(x, {y})
rubrics_metrics.description: Concatenate x and y horizontally (matrices) or treat non-vectors/matrices as 1-D vectors; if y omitted, concatenates elements of a row vector/list left-to-right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matrices concatenated horizontally (rows unchanged); use transposition or matconcat for vertical concatenation. Empty matrix [;] compatible with any operation; empty vectors are not. Examples show concatenation behaviors and Mat/matconcat shortcuts. Library syntax: GEN concat(GEN x, GEN y = NULL); GEN concat1 as shortcut.

rubrics_metrics.name: forqfvec(v, q, b, expr)
rubrics_metrics.description: Iterate expr over all integer vectors v with q(v) ≤ b, where q is a positive-definite quadratic form (square symmetric matrix).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal variable v runs through all such vectors; provides C-level interface variant allowing callback fun(E,v,m) returning 0 to continue or 1 to stop. Example prints vectors for q=[[3,2],[2,3]] and bound 3. Library syntax: void forqfvec0(GEN v, GEN q = NULL, GEN b) and void forqfvec(void *E, long (*fun)(void *, GEN, double), GEN q, GEN b).

rubrics_metrics.name: lindep(v, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Find a small non-trivial integer linear relation among components of vector v; returns empty vector if none found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For real/complex entries uses floating-point variable-precision LLL; flag=0 uses internal heuristic for accuracy, flag>0 sets accuracy in decimal digits (should be less than true input accuracy). For p-adic or matrix inputs behavior differs (p-adic uses lattice reduction; matrix returns kernel vector). For polynomial/power series inputs finds relation over base field; prefer t_POL inputs to avoid t-adic truncation issues. Example: lindep([sqrt(2),sqrt(3),sqrt(2)+sqrt(3)]) -> [-1,-1,1]. Library syntaxes: GEN lindep0, lindep, lindep2, padic_lindep, Xadic_lindep, deplin for matrices.

rubrics_metrics.name: listcreate()
rubrics_metrics.description: Create an empty list (t_LIST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obsolete: used to require argument but now ignored; function is redundant and will disappear—use List() instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: listinsert(L, x, n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Insert object x at position n in list L (t_LIST).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexity O(#L - n + 1) due to shifting elements. Library syntax: GEN listinsert(GEN L, GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: listkill(L)
rubrics_metrics.description: Obsolete routine retained for backward compatibility; previously removed list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use L = List() instead; local variables cleared automatically on function return. Library syntax: void listkill(GEN L).

rubrics_metrics.name: listpop(list, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Remove the n-th element of list (t_LIST); if n omitted or > length, removes last element. Does nothing if list empty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs in time O(#L - n + 1). Library syntax: void listpop(GEN list, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: listput(list, x, {n})
rubrics_metrics.description: Set n-th element of list to x; if n omitted or > length, append x. You may overwrite existing element (does not change length).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Runs in O(#L) worst-case (reallocation), O(1) amortized; multiple successive listputs cost O(#L) overall. Library syntax: GEN listput(GEN list, GEN x, long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: listsort(L, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Sort a t_LIST in place using universal comparison cmp; ordering same as sets allowing setsearch on a sorted list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster than vecsort since done in-place (no copy); no return value. If flag non-zero, suppress repeated coefficients (deduplicate). Library syntax: void listsort(GEN L, long flag).

rubrics_metrics.name: matadjoint(M, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute adjoint matrix (matrix of cofactors) N satisfying M*N = det(M)*Id for square M; M need not be invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses Leverrier-Faddeev (assumes n! invertible); if it fails or flag=1, compute characteristic polynomial first and evaluate formula (−1)^{n-1}(T(x)-T(0))/x at M. Both algorithms O(n^4) in base ring; often slower than computing charpoly or inverse. Library syntax: GEN matadjoint0(GEN M, long flag); aliases adj/ adjsafe.

rubrics_metrics.name: matcompanion(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the left companion matrix of the (non-zero) polynomial x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matcompanion(GEN x). No additional flags discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: matconcat(v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Build a matrix from entries of v: if v is t_VEC concatenate horizontally, t_COL vertically, t_MAT concatenate columns vertically; entries considered as matrices (scalars as 1×1 matrices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for block sizes: compute max row/column sizes of blocks to determine block dimensions; scalars expanded as scalar times identity of min(Hi,Lj); blocks extended by zeros as needed. Examples demonstrate horizontal, vertical, block and block-diagonal matrices. Library syntax: GEN matconcat(GEN v).

rubrics_metrics.name: matdet(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Determinant of square matrix x. Algorithm chosen depending on coefficient types and flag.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 (default) selects method: integer entries -> modular Dixon/Pernet/Stein; real/p-adic -> Gaussian elimination with max pivot; intmod -> Gaussian with first non-zero pivot; else Gauss-Bareiss. flag=1 forces classical Gaussian elimination with pivoting (usually worse). Library syntax: GEN det0(GEN x, long flag) and variants GEN det, det2, ZM_det for integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: matdetint(B)
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer m×n matrix B, compute determinant D of lattice generated by columns (sqrt(det(B^T B)) if B has full row rank, else 0).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses Gauss-Bareiss to compute positive multiple of D; when B square returns |det B|. Useful with mathnfmod which needs such multiple. For large m or n (>20) prefer mathnf alternatives. Library syntax: GEN detint(GEN B).

rubrics_metrics.name: matdiagonal(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create diagonal matrix with diagonal entries from vector x (or block-diagonal when entries are matrices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and use with matconcat to form block diagonal matrices. Library syntax: GEN diagonal(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: mateigen(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return eigenvectors of x as columns of a matrix (complex). If flag=1 return [L,H] (L eigenvalues, H eigenvectors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: compute charpoly, approximate complex roots λ_i, then compute kernels of x-λ_i; ill-conditioned, may miss kernel vectors if roots are close or multiple. For symmetric use qfjacobi; for Hermitian build real and imag blocks and apply qfjacobi. Library syntax: GEN mateigen(GEN x, long flag, long prec); alias eigen(GEN x, long prec) (flag=0).

rubrics_metrics.name: matfrobenius(M, {flag}, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return the Frobenius form of square M. flag=1 returns elementary divisors (vector of polynomials); flag=2 returns [F,B] with Frobenius form F and change-of-basis B (M = B^{-1} F B).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matfrobenius(GEN M, long flag, long v = -1).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathess(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a matrix similar to x in upper Hessenberg form (zeros below first subdiagonal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN hess(GEN x). Useful as intermediate for eigen/computation reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: mathilbert(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create Hilbert matrix of order n (coeff (i,j) = 1/(i+j-1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN mathilbert(long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathnf(M, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute Hermite Normal Form (HNF) over Euclidean ring R (Z or K[X]) of matrix M; returns upper triangular H such that columns form basis of module spanned by M's columns; flags control algorithms and output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag bits: 1 -> complete output [H,U] with transformation U (GL(R)); 2 deprecated (generic input polynomial assumption); flags >=4 choose different algorithms (4 uses LLL variant returning [H,U] with small U but slower; 5 uses Batut's algorithm returning [H,U,P] with permutation P, often faster). For dense large matrices, flag=4 fastest; when rank maximal, mathnfmod(M, matdetint(M)) can be faster and U recovered via M^{-1}H. Library syntax: GEN mathnf0(GEN M, long flag) and aliases hnf/hnfall. Notes about performance and large sparse matrices (hnfspec/hnfadd undocumented).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathnfmod(x, d)
rubrics_metrics.description: For integer-entry matrix x of maximal rank and d a multiple of determinant of lattice spanned by columns, compute upper triangular HNF of x using less memory (slower than mathnf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If rank equals number of rows result square; columns of result basis of column lattice. Use when memory is constrained. Library syntax: GEN hnfmod(GEN x, GEN d).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathnfmodid(x, d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Output HNF of x concatenated with diagonal matrix with diagonal d. If d integer, concatenate d times identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assumes x integer. Examples demonstrate both vector and scalar d. Library syntax: GEN hnfmodid(GEN x, GEN d).

rubrics_metrics.name: mathouseholder(Q, v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply sequence Q of Householder transforms (as returned by matqr(M,1)) to vector or matrix v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful because applying Householder sequence is more stable/faster than explicit multiplication by Q. Library syntax: GEN mathouseholder(GEN Q, GEN v).

rubrics_metrics.name: matid(n)
rubrics_metrics.description: Create n×n identity matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matid(long n).

rubrics_metrics.name: matimage(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a basis for the image (column space) of matrix x as columns of a matrix. Works for various entry types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses standard Gauss pivot (default); flag=1 uses matsupplement (much slower). Library syntax: GEN matimage0(GEN x, long flag); alias image(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matimagecompl(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return vector of column indices not extracted by matimage(x), as a permutation t_VECSMALL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Number of components plus number of columns in matimage(x) equals number of columns of x. Library syntax: GEN imagecompl(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matindexrank(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrix x of rank r, return vector with two t_VECSMALL components y and z listing row and column indices (1-based) such that the extracted submatrix vecextract(x,y,z) is invertible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to identify independent row/column sets. Library syntax: GEN indexrank(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matintersect(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrices x and y with same number of rows and independent columns, find basis of Q-vector space equal to intersection of column spaces of x and y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For fractional ideals use idealintersect (faster); for general ZK-modules use nfhnf (slower but general). Library syntax: GEN intersect(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matinverseimage(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrix x and column vector/matrix y, return a preimage z such that x*z = y if one exists; otherwise return empty vector/matrix. Complete inverse image is z + Ker(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples demonstrate solutions, no-solution cases, and multiple-column inputs. Use matker to get kernel basis. Library syntax: GEN inverseimage(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matisdiagonal(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return true (1) if x is diagonal matrix, false (0) otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN isdiagonal(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matker(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a basis for kernel of matrix x as columns of a matrix. Input entries can be any type compatible with +,*,/ operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If x known to have integral entries set flag=1 for optimized behavior. Library syntax: GEN matker0(GEN x, long flag); aliases ker/keri.

rubrics_metrics.name: matkerint(x, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return an LLL-reduced Z-basis for kernel lattice of integer matrix x (rational entries not permitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 uses integer LLL; flag=1 uses matrixqz(x,-2) (much slower; avoid). Library syntax: GEN matkerint0(GEN x, long flag); alias kerint. Implementation note: wraps ZM_lll routines; can remove outer LLL if not desired to save time.

rubrics_metrics.name: matmuldiagonal(x, d)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiply matrix x by diagonal matrix whose diagonal entries are in vector d; equivalent to x * matdiagonal(d) but much faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matmuldiagonal(GEN x, GEN d). Use when multiplying by diagonal matrices frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: matmultodiagonal(x, y)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute product of matrices x and y assuming the result is diagonal; much faster than general multiplication but undefined if result non-diagonal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only when you know x*y is diagonal. Library syntax: GEN matmultodiagonal(GEN x, GEN y).

rubrics_metrics.name: matpascal(n, {q})
rubrics_metrics.description: Create lower-triangular Pascal (binomial coefficients) matrix of order n+1. If q given compute q-Pascal triangle (q-binomial coefficients).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matqpascal(long n, GEN q = NULL); alias mat-pascal variants available.

rubrics_metrics.name: matqr(M, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute QR-decomposition [Q,R] of square invertible real matrix M with Q orthogonal and R upper-triangular. If flag=1 return Q as sequence of Householder transforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If flag=1 the returned Householder sequence can be applied via mathouseholder; it is stabler and faster. Function errors on low precision or singularity. Library syntax: GEN matqr(GEN M, long flag, long prec). Relationship: mathouseholder(q, matid(#M)) == Q^T and mathouseholder(q, M) == R when q from matqr(M,1).

rubrics_metrics.name: matrank(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return rank of matrix x.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: long rank(GEN x). No further flags in this description.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrix(m, n, {X}, {Y}, {expr = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Create m×n matrix whose coefficients are given by expression expr as function of formal parameters X (rows 1..m) and Y (cols 1..n). If last parameters omitted fill with zeros.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two formal parameters available: X (row index) and Y (column index). Useful for programmatic matrix construction. Library syntax reflected in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixqz(A, {p = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Transform rational m×n matrix A to integral matrix B with same Q-column-space and GCD of n×n minors coprime to p (if p≥0); other p values yield HNF bases of Zn∩ImZA (p=-1) or Zn∩ImQA (p=-2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If p≥0 assume A has maximal rank (n≤m) and return integral B with minors' GCD coprime to p (p=0 gives GCD 1). Examples show conversion of rational minors to integral matrix with coprime minors. Library syntax: GEN matrixqz0(GEN A, GEN p = NULL). Useful to clear denominators while controlling minors' gcd.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsize(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Return row vector [#rows, #columns] for vector or matrix x (row vector has 1 row, column vector 1 column).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN matsize(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: matsnf(X, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Return elementary divisors (diagonal of Smith Normal Form) of matrix X normalized dn | ... | d1. flag bits control output and input types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary digits of flag: 1 -> complete output [U,V,D] with unimodular U,V; 2 -> allow polynomial entries (square); 4 -> cleanup (delete elementary divisors equal to 1 and shorten outputs). If cleanup set, X may be given as vector of elementary divisors or full [U,V,D]. Library syntax: GEN matsnf0(GEN X, long flag). Handles rectangular matrices by padding diagonal matrix with zeros as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolve(M, B)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve M X = B for X when M invertible; uses Dixon p-adic lifting if M,B integral, Gaussian elimination otherwise (equivalent to M^{-1} * B but faster).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gauss(GEN M, GEN B) and integral variant ZM_gauss. Use for exact/integer linear solves for performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsolvemod(M, D, B, {flag = 0})
rubrics_metrics.description: Given integral matrix M, vector D of moduli, and integral B, find small integer solution x to congruence system Σ_i m_{i,j} x_j ≡ b_i (mod d_i) if exists; shorthand allows scalar D/B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: flag=0 returns small solution or zero if none; flag=1 returns all solutions as [x,u] where u columns give basis of homogeneous solutions. Examples provided. Library syntax: GEN matsolvemod0(GEN M, GEN D, GEN B, long flag); aliases gaussmodulo/gaussmodulo2.

rubrics_metrics.name: matsupplement(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given matrix x with linearly independent columns, find square invertible matrix whose first columns are columns of x (supplement to a basis of full space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raises error if x has 0 columns (design limitation). Example shows returned supplement. Library syntax: GEN suppl(GEN x). Use when completing a basis; matsupplement slower than matimage for some uses.

rubrics_metrics.name: mattranspose(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transpose of x (also x~). Effect applies only to vectors and matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN gtrans(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: minpoly(A, {v = x})
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimal polynomial of A with respect to variable v: monic polynomial P of minimal degree such that P(A)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Library syntax: GEN minpoly(GEN A, long v = -1). Useful to compute algebraic dependencies and as input to companion/matfrobenius routines.

rubrics_metrics.name: norml2(x)
rubrics_metrics.description: Square of L2-norm of x: for scalar the square modulus; for polynomials/vectors/matrices defined recursively as sum of norml2 over components (gives usual |xi|^2 or |xi,j|^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: norml2([1,2,3])=14; norml2([1,2;3,4])=30; norml2(2*I + x) = 5. Real t_QUAD not supported for scalars. Library syntax: GEN gnorml2(GEN x).

rubrics_metrics.name: normlp(x, {p})
rubrics_metrics.description: Lp-norm of x; sup norm if p omitted. For scalar normlp(x,p)=abs(x); for polynomials/vectors/matrices norm defined recursively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description truncated in chunk; general behavior: computes L^p norms with p parameter; for p omitted computes infinity norm (sup). Library syntax: implied GEN normlp(GEN x, GEN p).
